# Third-party sources: portal space (M2 wave 1)

The portal track ([m2-plan.md](../milestones/m2-plan.md) §3.3, "portal") owns `src/Lifestone.Data/Audio/`,
`src/Lifestone.Client/PortalSpace/`, `src/Lifestone.Client/Audio/` and their tests. **No third-party code is ported.**
Retail behaviour is re-expressed from the decompile, cited by function name with its 11.4186 and 11.6096 addresses;
nothing from the decompile is copied. Lifestone is AGPL-3.0, and every source below is compatible with that. Nothing
derived from the user's dats is committed.

It covers the whole track, steps PS1 to PS12; [portal-space.md](../portal-space.md) describes the design. The 11.6096
addresses are those of [retail-addresses-m2.md](../research/retail-addresses-m2.md) or, for functions that table does
not list, of the same pinned symbol table. Two functions have no 11.6096 address in it (§3 there): `DBWave::UnPack` and
`SoundTableData::Lookup` carry `TODO(portal): 11.6096` until the bytes are read: `SoundTableData::Lookup` is the
target of `CSoundTable::Lookup`'s forwarder at 11.6096 0x00552D20, and `DBWave::UnPack` the `UnPack` slot of the vtable
`DBWave::DBWave` (11.6096 0x005526C0) installs. Reading those bytes of `acclient.exe` is outside the inspection D4
approved (four constants), so it is left to the lead.
